conclusions: All9437184 bias/dtype/permutation comparisons complete with unchanged encoded inputs and memory guards. The zero-bias per-family counts and errors match the earlier intrinsic/isolated-assembly diagnostic. This confirms the new carry parameter does not change the control result.

For each dtype, zero bias has147981 fractional mismatches. Bias+262144 leaves29722 mismatches and bias-262144 leaves29825. Biases+/-1048576,+/-4194304 and+/-12582912 have zero mismatches in every tested family, including mixed-sign K2/K4/K8/K16 and exact cancellation.

The native WMMA receives an exactly representable constant in C. Host FP64 subtraction of that integer from the bounded FP32 result is exact and every resulting value is compared directly to the independent int64 dot. No nearest-integer conversion, fitted error correction or changed rounding mode participates.

The largest tested bias,3*2^22, leaves each mathematically expected result in one FP32 exponent bin for this bounded operand domain, with unit spacing. This is an analytical range observation, not a proof of undocumented WMMA internal arithmetic.

This finite result warrants a broader signed-core stress experiment, including extrema and reconstructed16-bit Karatsuba products, before considering full captured QK/projection timing. It does not prove a universal integer primitive or qualify a model, provider, performance target or release.
